However, Maye also threw three interceptions, all coming in the first half. Green Bay capitalized on the turnovers, building a 24-14 halftime lead after taking advantage of New England's early mistakes. item.title: Another QB injury: Drew Lock’s status ‘up in the air’ for Week 10 vs. Raiders
item.description: It might be Jalen Milroe time for the Seattle Seahawks. While Drew Lock didn’t miss any game action during Seattle’s 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals, he has a new injury on top of the severe tendinitis he reportedly had been battling over the past couple of weeks. Lock was seen grabbing his right hip area during the third quarter of Sunday’s game, grimacing and walking gingerly as he got off the field prior to Seattle’s final scoring drive. Jalen Milroe warmed up on the sidelines while Lock went into the blue tent, but Lock stayed in for the rest of the afternoon and didn’t miss a play. Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald told reporters at the post-game press conference that Lock’s status is “up in the air” after getting his oblique looked at. “We’re looking at him for an oblique, so we’ll assess it and go from there,” Macdonald said. “He made it out [of the game], but you know, like I’ve sat here before and told you a guy would be ready and then he wasn’t. So, leave my options open.” For what it’s worth, Lock said “we’ll get it looked at [Sunday night]” and that it “was not too bad.” When asked if the injury affected him, he said, “I wouldn’t say it did.” The Seahawks talk about having a “70-man roster,” knowing they’ll frequently need contributions from beyond the 53. With six starters down, this was one of those weeks. Mike Macdonald said it showed “the power of our 70” and called Drew Lock “a beast” for playing through injury. pic.twitter.com/rp7ZM3vgeo — Brady Henderson (@BradyHenderson) November 9, 2026 Lock also said he felt “good” playing through the elbow injury. Odds are not sounding favorable for Sam Darnold to return against the Las Vegas Raiders, with ESPN’s Adam Schefter reporting what felt like a pretty obvious situation that he is in “jeopardy” of missing Week 10 with quad and rib injuries. If Darnold was listed as “week-to-week” by Mike Macdonald, this isn’t earth-shattering news as much as it affirms what’s already been said. If the news is negative on Lock, then we could see Jalen Milroe’s first career NFL start. But at the minimum, this is a very banged up Seahawks quarterback room and the bye week might be one of the most welcome byes in recent Seahawks history.

item.title: Jordan Love, Packers offense give Patriots' $135 million cornerback nightmares
item.description: The passes arc with a sense of predetermination these days when Jordan Love uncorks another deep ball. The intended target is certainly going to have a chance to catch the ball, and odds are he has some degree of separation against the doomed coverage. What’s less of a guarantee is whether the pass catcher will perform his duty and complete the grab, but that was not an issue during the Packers ’ 45-27 victory over the New England Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 8. The numbers are cartoonish, as Green Bay put up a season high in points and total yards (478) – the worst rushing team in the NFL entering the week scored three times on the ground and ran for 129 yards with running back Josh Jacobs sidelined for most of the game after suffering a broken finger. Love finished with 372 yards passing and three scores through the air and added a rushing touchdown to kick off the scoring 101 seconds into the game to create a well-balanced stat sheet. The one-two punch in the wide-receiver room of Christian Watson and Matthew Golden showed out with a combined 17 receptions on 18 targets for 335 yards and two touchdowns. “It’s bombs away,” NBC’s Jason Garrett said during “Football Night in America.” Fellow NBC analyst Mike Tomlin said it was time to consider the tandem among the elite duos in the league “at the tip-top of the food chain.” Mike Vrabel criticizes Christian Gonzalez after Patriots' loss The performance put Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel in position to criticize one of his best players in cornerback Christian Gonzalez. Signed to a four-year, $135 million extension that made him one of the richest corners in the NFL, Gonzalez was targeted by Love 11 times. He was successful on 10 of those occasions, for 187 yards and a touchdown. “When your best players don’t play well, it’s hard to win in this league,” Vrabel said. The 2025 Coach of the Year continued: “We expect a lot more. He expects a lot more. We need more from him and everybody else. It wasn't just him. Again, we got to be able to coach and be prepared, and then we have to execute. Just like it is every single week when we don't win, it's all of us, and it starts with me.” By the end of the first quarter, Golden had 126 receiving yards. Love completed seven passes that went for 24 yards or more and averaged 12.8 yards per attempt. He was 6-for-8 on deep passes (20+ air yards) for 235 yards and a touchdown, according to Next Gen Stats. It marked the second time Love completed six deep passes this season (Week 5 against the Chicago Bears was the other) – no other quarterback in the NFL has done it once in 2026. "It feels like you're in that flow state and just finding ways to get guys the ball ... it's a great feeling, and you just want to keep chasing every play and keep making good plays," Love told reporters. item.title: Coco Gauff powers past Jessica Pegula in WTA Finals opener
item.description: FILE PHOTO - US tennis player Coco Gauff in action against Czech's Karolina Muchova during their women's singles semi-final match on day eleven of the 2026 Wimbledon Championships at the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club, London. (is associated with: «Coco Gauff powers past Jessica Pegula in WTA Finals opener») Mike Egerton/PA Wire/dpa Coco Gauff overcame Jessica Pegula 6-4, 6-7 (5-7), 6-2 with a dominant third-set display to open her WTA Finals campaign. The world number four took the opener and recovered from 5-1 down in the second to come within a point of winning in straight sets. But it was Pegula’s turn to dig in from 5-6, saving a match point and then playing a terrific tie-break to extend the contest at Indian Wells. Gauff took charge of the match in the third set, breaking to lead 3-0 before earning her sixth win against Pegula after two hours and 39 minutes. Pegula would probably have been grateful to get the tennis under way after her viral and awkward ‘hot mic’ moment when disparaging comments she made about fellow player Mirra Andreeva to her coach during a training session were picked up on a livestream. That prompted a grovelling apology from the WTA, which admitted it had not told players the microphones were on, and damage control behind the scenes from Pegula. The world number five had compared Andreeva’s mentality unfavourably with Gauff’s in her indiscreet comments, and the two-time grand slam champion set about showing her competitive grit, clawing her way back with five games in a row, including saving three set points. Sometime doubles partners Gauff and Pegula had shared their 10 previous meetings, while this was the fourth year in a row they were meeting at the WTA Finals. Earlier, Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova marked her debut with a 6-2, 6-4 victory against alternate Marta Kostyuk. Kostyuk received a late call-up after world number one Elena Rybakina pulled out through illness, but it was Czech Noskova who came out on top.

item.title: 5 takeaways as Patriots lose in embarrassing fashion to Green Bay Packers
item.description: FOXBOROUGH – Gillette Stadium was rocking on Sunday. Before the Patriots ’ matchup with the Green Bay Packers , the organization honored the tenth anniversary of their 2016 Super Bowl team. The pre-game festivities saw several players from that team come onto the field for a short ceremony. Adding to the atmosphere was Tom Brady, who was up in the TV booth as a color commentator for Fox Sports. On top of that, Rob Gronkowski was being honored at halftime after being inducted into the Patriots Hall of Fame. The home crowd was buzzing until the game started. That’s when the Patriots ran into a buzzsaw and sleepwalked through a terrible, no-good, very bad first quarter. The Gillette Stadium crowd was booing the Patriots at various points throughout the first half. Those boos continued Sunday as Mike Vrabel’s team was dominated from start to finish in this embarrassing 45-27 loss to the Packers. The 45 points allowed is the most by a Patriots team since 1990. The Patriots fell to 5-4 with a matchup against the Detroit Lions in Munich on deck. Here’s what happened: First quarter was abysmal The Patriots offense didn’t start fast on Sunday. Neither did the defense. The offense’s first two plays were disastrous as Drake Maye’s group helped the Packers take an early 7-0 lead. It took the Packers no time to take a 14-0 lead in a woeful first quarter. The offense’s first play of the game was an illegal shift penalty. Their second was even worse as Maye was easily intercepted by Packers safety Xavier McKinney at 14:32 of the first quarter. Maye was trying to connect with Mack Hollins, but threw the ball right to McKinney, who ran back 36 yards and set Green Bay up at the 14-yard line. It took the Packers two plays to get into the end zone with quarterback Jordan Love running in a 13-yard touchdown at 13:19 of the first quarter. After the Patriots went three-and-out in their next series, the Packers beat up on the defense. Love completed a 49-yard pass to Matthew Golden, setting up Green Bay at the 18-yard line. Next, Christian Gonzalez was called for a pass interference penalty, which negated an interception he had. That set Green Bay up at the 9-yard line. Two plays later, Golden was left wide open for an easy 5-yard touchdown pass at 7:59 of this no-good, very bad first quarter. To make it even more disappointing, Kyle Williams had a chance to make a 47-yard touchdown catch but the receiver misjudged the deep ball, slowed down and the ball fell between his outstretched fingers in the end zone at 5:38 of the first quarter. The first quarter ended with fans inside Gillette Stadium booing. Second quarter didn’t start much better The Patriots secondary and their top cornerback had a world of issues on Sunday. item.title: Patriots' already-thin offense takes another hit vs. Packers
item.description: FOXBOROUGH — An already-thin running back room got thinner on Sunday for the Patriots against the Packers . Rhamondre Stevenson suffered a knee injury in the third quarter and was ruled out. Stevenson remained down after a play, but walked off the field and into the blue medical tent. He eventually made his way to the locker room for further evaluation. The Patriots were down 42-21 when Stevenson was ruled out. It’s possible it was just precautionary due to the score. With TreVeyon Henderson (illness) out for the foreseeable future, the Patriots can ill-afford to lose another running back, especially with A.J. Brown (knee, ankle) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder) out. It’s unclear when the trio will return. Stevenson lost a fumble in the third quarter. The Packers scored a touchdown on the first play of the drive after the recovery. Before the injury, Stevenson had six carries for 32 rushing yards to go with three receptions, 46 receiving yards and a touchdown. Jokic has played in all eight games for Denver, which improved to 5-3 with Saturday’s 114-102 win over the Indiana Pacers in Mexico City. Now he’s one of six Nuggets listed as questionable on the NBA’s Sunday injury report. That group includes all five players who started against Indiana. Nikola Jokic’s Elbow Injury Follows an Up-and-Down Shooting Start Jokic went 7-for-20 from the floor against Indiana, finishing with 19 points, 13 rebounds and eight assists in 36 minutes. Three days earlier, he went 13-for-19 in a win over Toronto and finished with 32 points, 10 rebounds and 11 assists. The two performances capture how much his scoring efficiency has swung through Denver’s first eight games. It started on opening night, when Jokic scored 13 points on 5-for-19 shooting against Oklahoma City. He followed that with 35 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists against New Orleans. Through eight games, he’s averaging 22.9 points, 10.1 rebounds and 9.1 assists, according to his CBS Sports game log. The elbow sprain adds a new question to those shooting swings. Denver’s report gives no date for the injury, so it’s unclear whether the elbow was bothering Jokic during any of those games. Even on the tougher shooting nights, the rest of his game has held up. He had 11 assists against Golden State on Oct. 26 and was two assists shy of a triple-double against Indiana. item.title: Every player from California to play for the Brooklyn Nets - Corey Gaines
item.description: The Brooklyn Nets have signed, drafted, and traded for players from virtually every state in the US, and much of the wider world beyond the United States. From Alabama to Wyoming, and from Australia to Ukraine, the Nets have a long and distinguished history of turning over every stone to find the talent needed to succeed in the NBA. From their start in the American Basketball Association (ABA) as the New Jersey Americans and New York Nets to their jump to the NBA as the New Jersey Nets right through to today, the organization has cast their net for talent wide since the inception of the ball club. item.title: How Carlos Alcaraz and Rafael Nadal performed on their ATP Finals debuts as Rafael Jodar qualifies for 2026 event
item.description: Rafael Jodar has achieved the unthinkable. The Spanish starlet has qualified for the ATP Finals, despite only turning professional at the start of this year . Jodar secured the eighth and final ATP Finals qualification spot following Carlos Alcaraz’s stunning comeback victory against Taylor Fritz in the Paris Masters quarter-finals. Speaking of Alcaraz, let’s take a look at how the Spanish magician – and fellow Spanish tennis legend Rafael Nadal – fared on his ATP Finals debut. Carlos Alcaraz’s ATP Finals debut Alcaraz qualified for the 2022 ATP Finals after winning his first Grand Slam title at the 2022 US Open. Unfortunately for the Spaniard, he was ultimately forced to withdraw from the event due to injury. Alcaraz again qualified in 2023, and on this occasion, injury would not prevent the Spaniard from making his tournament debut. Alcaraz, seeded second at the 2023 ATP Finals, advanced to the semi-finals after defeating Daniil Medvedev and Andrey Rublev in the group stage. Novak Djokovic swiftly ended Alcaraz’s hopes of a debut triumph, winning their semi-final contest 6-3, 6-2. “Best match of the tournament for me without a doubt,” Djokovic said afterwards. “It came at the right time, really, after spending a lot of hours on the court in the first three matches. I didn’t know how I’m going to feel. Carlos Alcaraz’s 2026 ATP Finals campaign Group stage: defeated Daniil Medvedev 6-4, 6-4 Group stage: defeated Andrey Rublev 7-5, 6-2 Group stage: lost to Alexander Zverev, 7-6, 3-6, 4-6 Semi-finals: lost to Novak Djokovic 3-6, 2-6 “But tonight from the very beginning I felt the ball well. I was approaching the match with the right attitude, right mentality.” Djokovic went on to win a record-breaking seventh ATP Finals title, beating Jannik Sinner in the final. Rafael Nadal’s ATP Finals debut Nadal, a 22-time Grand Slam champion, made his ATP Finals [then the Tennis Masters Cup] debut in 2006. Like Alcaraz, the Spanish superstar reached the semi-finals, beating Nikolay Davydenko and Tommy Robredo en route. Nadal, who qualified second in his group behind eighth seed James Blake, was beaten by Roger Federer in the semi-finals. Photo by FREDERIC J. BROWN / AFP via Getty Images “I am satisfied for finish the season with my best game, satisfied for that, because you finish the season with a very good feelings. That’s very important. And I am satisfied with my semifinal, yes,” Nadal said during his post-match press conference. “I win two matches against the two top eight players. And I lost against the No. 1 now today, but playing at very good level and good match, no? “So I am happy with the tournament, yes.” As for Federer, the Swiss star went on to the win the title in Shanghai, China, defeating James Blake in the final. The occasion marked Federer’s third ATP Finals title. Federer went on to win six titles in total, the last being in 2011. Despite reaching the final on two occasions, Nadal never won the ATP Finals.

item.title: Did Hansi Flick get it right in Barcelona’s victory over Atletico Madrid?
item.description: Atletico Madrid's Argentine coach Diego Simeone hugs Barcelona's German coach Hans-Dieter Flick prior the Spanish league football match between Club Atletico de Madrid and FC Barcelona at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid on November 8, 2026. (Photo by Javier SORIANO / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images When you play Diego Simeone’s Atletico Madrid away from home , coming out of the lion’s den with a win is a plus no matter how you look at it. For Hansi Flick, there was also an opportunity to prove he learned his lessons against a team that had his number last season. Had Barcelona lost this game, which they very certainly could have, the chorus of criticism would have reached a fever pitch for a team that had already fallen to Real Madrid and PSG in recent weeks. The current coaching conditions are tough for Flick. His roster coming into the day continued to be light on good defensive options. That being said, help was on the way with Andreas Christensen and Eric Garcia making it back into the roster. Flick had choices to make, and in the end, he doubled down on his known biases. When I saw the starting eleven, I immediately felt cause for concern. Atleti has been one of the best teams at getting behind Barca’s backline, and Flick sent out João Cancelo and Brian Fariñas as his full-backs. A non-defending defender, and an academy midfielder deputizing as a full-back. In addition to that, he chose to play Marc Bernal instead of Frenkie de Jong in place of the injured Rodri. For me, the first half was a horror show. Simeone got everything right, while all Flick could do was pray for half-time to make changes. Luckily, Julián Alvarez missed a wide open opportunity to make it 2-0, and then Fermín López came to the rescue to even things up right before half-time, which totally changed the dynamic of the game. At the break, player changes were obviously needed for Barcelona. Flick made the right choice to bring in Frenkie de Jong, but the surprise choice of playing him as a full-back in place of Fariñas. It needs to be asked, what’s really going on with Alejandro Balde? At the moment, it looks like he’s completely locked out of the lineup with no chance back in on merit, and the sad part is, that decision is costing the team. Balde, I think many people would argue, would have been a better option than Cancelo in this game because it was a matchup that demanded physicality and good defending. Furthermore, all you ask of a coach is to be fair. When everyone is getting in front of your starting full-back from last season, no matter how many others fall to injury and fatigue, the coach must give a clear explanation, otherwise it’s starts to smell like personal feelings are coming before what’s in the best interest of the team. Fermín López was the man of the hour again. He’s the player that never quits, and it made all the difference against Atleti. item.title: LeBron James shines as Sixers down Bulls
item.description: Veteran superstar LeBron James scored 22 points with five assists, returning to form (Michael Reaves) LeBron James had his best game yet for the Philadelphia 76ers, who bounced back with a 127-121 win in Chicago on Sunday over a Bulls side that has now lost seven straight NBA games. Veteran superstar James scored 22 points -- his highest tally since joining the Sixers this summer -- and a return to form after a paltry eight points in Friday's disappointing loss to Cleveland. James also had five assists while Jaylen Brown top-scored with 29, Tyrese Maxey poured in 27 and Joel Embiid pulled down 10 rebounds. The star-studded Sixers have lost just twice so far this season, for their best start after 11 games since 2000. Philadelphia grabbed the lead early in the second quarter and never trailed from there, though a resilient Chicago pulled within two points in the closing stages. "We have a lot of guys that's been in situations, late-game situations, and we have a 'no panic' button," said James. "We understand that we got to get stops on this end, but if teams make a run, we understand how to be calm on the other end as well." The Bulls remain joint-bottom of the Eastern Conference with the Milwaukee Bucks -- the only team Chicago has beaten so far this campaign. They were without shooting guard Norman Powell, their second-leading scorer this season, who was placed on the injury report hours before tip-off with back discomfort. But Josh Giddey provided some hope with a double-double including 19 points and 15 assists. Meanwhile, James' former Los Angeles Lakers team overcame the absence of red-hot talisman Luka Doncic to beat the Detroit Pistons 121-116, and also move to 9-2. Doncic, who has been averaging more than 40 points per game this season, was left out with lower back tightness, the team announced. Austin Reaves stepped up, scoring 43 points, including two calm free throws in the final seconds to take the game beyond Detroit's reach. The Lakers never trailed but had to fight hard to retain a razor-thin lead for most of the fourth quarter.
